As a manager working for an inclusive environment, you want to demonstrate to your employees everyone has the ability to express valuable contributions. 

### Assess the environment and level of participation
To do this, you first need to focus on providing a safe environment for productive and positive conversations. Group meetings, one-on-one meetings, or department townhalls need to be inviting spaces where employees feel comfortable and safe to express their insights. If you notice a lack of participation, have individual conversations with your employees and find out if they have specific concerns or feel barriers to sharing their thoughts. Manage your team dynamics so that certain vocal members don't overly dominate conversations.

### Remind them about the value of diversity in creative thinking 
Make it a case to remind your employees about the role of diversity of thought and experience in the formulation of ideas. The greater number of perspectives, the richer the collective idea. Explain how their opinions matter in the formation of a greater overall idea. Ensure that they feel safe to volunteer any ideas, no matter how "crazyâ€ they may be to others.
     
Read this [article](https://www.inc.com/adam-robinson/4-ways-to-encourage-honest-employee-feedback-and-turn-it-into-action.html) on suggestions for encouraging feedback.
